akhfash:9-9.t: He said ﴿قُلْ مَا كُنتُ بِدْعاً مِّنَ ٱلرُّسُلِ﴾: "البِدْع" is the novel one (البديع), i.e. the first.

akhfash:12-12.t:
And He said ﴿وَمِن قَبْلِهِ كِتَابُ مُوسَىٰ إِمَاماً وَرَحْمَةً﴾: accusative because it is the khabar of a definite (i.e. a ḥāl).
And He said ﴿وَهَـٰذَا كِتَابٌ مُّصَدِّقٌ لِّسَاناً عَرَبِيّاً﴾: He put "tongue" and "Arabic" in the accusative because it is not an attribute of "the Book"; it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), or by an implied verb, as though He said: "I mean an Arabic tongue". Some said its accusative is by "مُصَدِّق" (confirming): he made the Book the confirmer of the tongue.

akhfash:33-33.t: As for His word ﴿وَلَمْ يَعْيَ بِخَلْقِهِنَّ بِقَادِرٍ عَلَىٰ أَن يُحْيِـيَ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ﴾, it is with the bāʾ like the bāʾ in His word ﴿كَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ﴾, and it is like ﴿تَنبُتُ بِٱلدُّهْنِ﴾.

akhfash:35-35.t: And He said ﴿لَمْ يَلْبَثُوۤاْ إِلاَّ سَاعَةً مِّن نَّهَارٍ بَلاَغٌ﴾: He means "that is a proclamation". Some said: "The proclamation is the Quran", and admonition is only by the Quran. Then He said ﴿بَلاَغٌ﴾, i.e. it is a proclamation.

daas-irab:1-5.t: ﴿حم﴾ ﴿تَنْزِيلُ الْكِتابِ مِنَ اللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَكِيمِ﴾ their i'rab has preceded in Sūrat al-Jāthiya. ﴿ما خَلَقْنَا﴾ mā is negative, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ its object. ﴿وَالْأَرْضَ﴾ conjoined to al-samāwāt. ﴿وَما﴾ conjoined to al-arḍ. ﴿بَيْنَهُما﴾ an adverb of place (ẓarf makān). ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause mā khalaqnā is resumptive. ﴿وَأَجَلٍ﴾ conjoined to al-ḥaqq. ﴿مُسَمًّى﴾ an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ a resumptive particle, and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿عَمَّا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to muʿriḍūn. ﴿أُنْذِرُوا﴾ a passive past verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the ṣila. ﴿مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of alladhīna; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿أَرَأَيْتُمْ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle of rebuke (tawbīkh), and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿ما﴾ its object; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿تَدْعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿أَرُونِي﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil, the nūn is for protection (al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ of the speaker is its object; the clause arūnī is a tawkīd (emphasis). ﴿ماذا﴾ a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of khalaqū. ﴿خَلَقُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿مِنَ الْأَرْضِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl; the clause mādhā khalaqū is the second object of a-raʾaytum. ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction in the sense of bal, for digression (iḍrāb). ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, a fronted khabar. ﴿شِرْكٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to shirk. ﴿ائْتُونِي﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil, the nūn is for protection, and the yāʾ of the speaker is a mafʿūl bihi. ﴿بِكِتابٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective of kitāb. ﴿هذا﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿أَثارَةٍ﴾ conjoined to kitāb. ﴿مِنْ عِلْمٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective of athāra. ﴿إِنْ﴾ a conditional particle causing the jussive. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿صادِقِينَ﴾ its khabar; the verbal clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ a resumptive particle, and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿أَضَلُّ﴾ khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مِمَّنْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to aḍallu. ﴿يَدْعُوا﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a mafʿūl bihi of yadʿū. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يَسْتَجِيبُ﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the ṣila of man. ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿إِلى يَوْمِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿عَنْ دُعائِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ghāfilūn. ﴿غافِلُونَ﴾ the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:6-8.t: ﴿وَإِذا﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and idhā is an adverbial conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿حُشِرَ النَّاسُ﴾ a passive past verb and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أَعْداءً﴾ the khabar (predicate) of kānū; the clause kānū is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَكانُوا﴾ a conjunction, and kāna and its noun. ﴿بِعِبادَتِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar kāfirīn; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿كافِرِينَ﴾ the khabar of kāna. ﴿وَإِذا﴾ like the preceding one. ﴿تُتْلى﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿آياتُنا﴾ nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿بَيِّناتٍ﴾ ḥāl; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿قالَ الَّذِينَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿لِلْحَقِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to qāla. ﴿لَمَّا﴾ adverbial, of time (ḥīniyya). ﴿جاءَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿هذا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar, and mubīn is an adjective (ṣifa); the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿أَمْ﴾ a conjunction in the sense of bal. ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿افْتَراهُ﴾ a past verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent; the clause is the object of the saying, and the clause yaqūlūna is resumptive. ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿إِنِ﴾ conditional. ﴿افْتَرَيْتُهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ falls in the apodosis of the condition, and lā is negative. ﴿تَمْلِكُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, and the clause qul is resumptive. ﴿لِي﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to the verb. ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿هُوَ أَعْلَمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿بِما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to aʿlamu. ﴿تُفِيضُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿فِيهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila of mā. ﴿كَفى﴾ a past verb. ﴿بِهِ﴾ the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and the hāʾ is a pronoun in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil of kafā. ﴿شَهِيداً﴾ tamyīz (specification). ﴿بَيْنِي﴾ an adverb of place (ẓarf makān). ﴿وَبَيْنَكُمْ﴾ conjoined to baynī. ﴿وَهُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ and two khabars; the clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:9-11.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿ما﴾ negative. ﴿كُنْتُ﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿بِدْعاً﴾ its khabar (predicate); the verbal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause qul is resumptive. ﴿مِنَ الرُّسُلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) bidʿan. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and mā is negative. ﴿أَدْرِي﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent, and the clause is circumstantial. ﴿ما﴾ interrogative, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يُفْعَلُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb; its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent, and the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿بِي﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the nominal clause stands in place of the two objects of adrī. ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and lā is negative. ﴿بِكُمْ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِنْ﴾ negative. ﴿أَتَّبِعُ﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿يُوحى﴾ a passive imperfect verb; its nāʾib fāʿil is latent. ﴿إِلَيَّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and mā is negative. ﴿أَنَا﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction. ﴿نَذِيرٌ﴾ khabar. ﴿مُبِينٌ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of nadhīr; the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿أَرَأَيْتُمْ﴾ the hamza is for interrogation, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the object of the saying, and the clause qul is resumptive. ﴿إِنْ﴾ a conditional particle causing the jussive. ﴿كانَ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿مِنْ عِنْدِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of kāna. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿وَكَفَرْتُمْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿وَشَهِدَ شاهِدٌ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿مِنْ بَنِي﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to shāhid. ﴿إِسْرائِيلَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَلى مِثْلِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to shahida. ﴿فَآمَنَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿وَاسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يَهْدِي﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿الْقَوْمَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ an adjective; the clause yahdī is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ﴾ a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to qāla. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿لَوْ﴾ a conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿كانَ خَيْراً﴾ kāna and its khabar, its noun being latent; the clause is initial. ﴿ما﴾ negative. ﴿سَبَقُونا﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object. ﴿إِلَيْهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَإِذْ﴾ an adverb for past time. ﴿لَمْ يَهْتَدُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lam, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿فَسَيَقُولُونَ﴾ a conjunction, the sīn is for the future, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿هذا إِفْكٌ قَدِيمٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar, and qadīm is an adjective; the nominal clause is the object of the saying.

daas-irab:12-14.t: ﴿وَمِنْ﴾ a resumptive particle, and min is a preposition. ﴿قَبْلِهِ﴾ a genitive noun; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿كِتابُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مُوسى﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿إِماماً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَرَحْمَةً﴾ conjoined to imāman; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَهذا كِتابٌ﴾ a conjunction, and a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. ﴿مُصَدِّقٌ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿لِساناً﴾ ḥāl. ﴿عَرَبِيًّا﴾ an adjective; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لِيُنْذِرَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit an after the lām of causation (taʿlīl); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to muṣaddiq. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿ظَلَمُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَبُشْرى﴾ the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. ﴿لِلْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to bushrā; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّ﴾ ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the ṣila, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿رَبُّنَا اللَّهُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿اسْتَقامُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to qālū. ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and lā is negative. ﴿خَوْفٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is the khabar of inna. ﴿وَلا﴾ a conjunction, and lā is negative. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَحْزَنُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. ﴿الْجَنَّةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿خالِدِينَ﴾ ḥāl. ﴿فِيها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to khālidīn. ﴿جَزاءً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb. ﴿بِما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to jazāʾan. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of kānū, and the clause ulāʾika… is a second khabar of inna.

daas-irab:15-16.t: ﴿وَوَصَّيْنَا﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿الْإِنْسانَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive. ﴿بِوالِدَيْهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿إِحْساناً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb. ﴿حَمَلَتْهُ﴾ a past verb and its object. ﴿أُمُّهُ﴾ a postponed fāʿil. ﴿كُرْهاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl). ﴿وَوَضَعَتْهُ كُرْهاً﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَحَمْلُهُ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿وَفِصالُهُ﴾ conjoined to ḥamluhu. ﴿ثَلاثُونَ﴾ khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw. ﴿شَهْراً﴾ tamyīz (specification). ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of beginning (ibtidāʾ). ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverbial conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿بَلَغَ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿أَشُدَّهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa), and the clause ﴿وَبَلَغَ أَرْبَعِينَ﴾ is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿سَنَةً﴾ tamyīz. ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the apodosis of a condition that does not cause the jussive, and has no grammatical position. ﴿رَبِّ﴾ the one addressed (munādā), annexed to the omitted yāʾ of the speaker. ﴿أَوْزِعْنِي﴾ a verb of supplication; its fāʿil is latent, the nūn is for protection (al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَنْ أَشْكُرَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an, with its fāʿil latent; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of the accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi of awziʿnī. ﴿نِعْمَتَكَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi of ashkura. ﴿الَّتِي﴾ an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿أَنْعَمْتَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿عَلَيَّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَعَلى والِدَيَّ﴾ conjoined to what precedes them. ﴿وَأَنْ أَعْمَلَ صالِحاً﴾ conjoined to an ashkura niʿmataka. ﴿تَرْضاهُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent; the clause is an adjective of ʿamalan. [Translator's note: so in the source; the word in the verse is صالِحاً.] ﴿وَأَصْلِحْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and the verb is conjoined to awziʿnī. ﴿لِي﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿فِي ذُرِّيَّتِي﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿إِنِّي﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿تُبْتُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation. ﴿إِلَيْكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿وَإِنِّي﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and inna and its noun. ﴿مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of inna; the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. ﴿نَتَقَبَّلُ﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿أَحْسَنَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿ما﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿عَمِلُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَنَتَجاوَزُ عَنْ سَيِّئاتِهِمْ﴾ conjoined to nataqabbalu, and ﴿فِي أَصْحابِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿الْجَنَّةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَعْدَ﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿الصِّدْقِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ an adjective. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿يُوعَدُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the khabar of kānū, and the clause kānū is the ṣila of alladhī.

daas-irab:17-19.t: ﴿وَالَّذِي﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿لِوالِدَيْهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of alladhī. ﴿أُفٍّ﴾ a verbal noun (ism fiʿl) of the imperfect, in the sense of "I am vexed" (ataḍajjaru). ﴿لَكُما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to uffin. ﴿أَتَعِدانِنِي﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil and its object. ﴿أَنْ أُخْرَجَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of taʿidāninī. ﴿وَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and qad is a particle of realization (taḥqīq). ﴿خَلَتِ﴾ a past verb. ﴿الْقُرُونُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِي﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is circumstantial. ﴿وَهُما﴾ the wāw is circumstantial, and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَسْتَغِيثانِ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the alif is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of humā, and the nominal clause is circumstantial. ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَيْلَكَ﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb. ﴿آمِنْ﴾ an imperative verb; its fāʿil is latent, and the clause āmin is the object of an implied saying. ﴿إِنَّ وَعْدَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). [Translator's note: the source prints the word with a fatḥa (اللَّهَ); as muḍāf ilayhi it is اللَّهِ.] ﴿حَقٌّ﴾ the khabar of inna; the nominal clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl). ﴿فَيَقُولُ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿ما﴾ negative. ﴿هذا﴾ mubtadaʾ; the verbal clause is conjoined to the implied clause before it. [Translator's note: this remark on the verbal clause evidently refers to fa-yaqūlu; it stands here in the source.] ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿أَساطِيرُ﴾ khabar. ﴿الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ its khabar; the nominal clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of alladhī in the previous verse. ﴿حَقَّ﴾ a past verb. ﴿عَلَيْهِمُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿الْقَوْلُ﴾ a postponed fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿فِي أُمَمٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿قَدْ﴾ a particle of realization. ﴿خَلَتْ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil is latent, and the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of umam. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿مِنَ الْجِنِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿وَالْإِنْسِ﴾ conjoined to al-jinn. ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿خاسِرِينَ﴾ its khabar; the verbal clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation. ﴿وَلِكُلٍّ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and li-kullin is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿دَرَجاتٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مِمَّا﴾ an adjective of darajāt. ﴿عَمِلُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَلِيُوَفِّيَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb, accusative by an implicit an after the lām of causation, with its fāʿil latent, and the hāʾ is its first object. ﴿أَعْمالَهُمْ﴾ its second object; the interpreted maṣdar from an and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and they [the preposition and its genitive noun] are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "He requited them" (jāzāhum). ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial, and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يُظْلَمُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:20-21.t: ﴿وَيَوْمَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān). ﴿يُعْرَضُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿عَلَى النَّارِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) yuʿraḍu; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). [Translator's note: so in the source; the remark on the ṣila evidently belongs to kafarū.] ﴿أَذْهَبْتُمْ طَيِّباتِكُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object. ﴿فِي حَياتِكُمُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to adhhabtum; the clause is the object of an implied saying (maqūl qawl muqaddar). ﴿الدُّنْيا﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of ḥayātikum. ﴿وَاسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ﴾ a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَالْيَوْمَ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and an adverb of time. ﴿تُجْزَوْنَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿عَذابَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿الْهُونِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive. ﴿بِما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to tujzawna. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿تَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of kuntum, and the clause kuntum is the ṣila. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿بِغَيْرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿الْحَقِّ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَبِما كُنْتُمْ تَفْسُقُونَ﴾ conjoined to bi-mā kuntum. ﴿وَاذْكُرْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿أَخا﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿عادٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِذْ﴾ a badal (substitute) of akhā ʿĀd. ﴿أَنْذَرَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿قَوْمَهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, with the fāʿil latent; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿بِالْأَحْقافِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿وَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and qad is a particle of realization (taḥqīq). ﴿خَلَتِ النُّذُرُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿مِنْ بَيْنِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to khalat. ﴿يَدَيْهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes them. ﴿أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوا﴾ an is lightened from the heavy anna, and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); lā is prohibitive, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to andhara. ﴿أَلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). [Translator's note: the source prints the word as أَلَّا; the particle of restriction in the verse is إِلَّا.] ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿إِنِّي﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿أَخافُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, its fāʿil latent; the clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl) of the worship. ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿عَذابَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿يَوْمٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَظِيمٍ﴾ an adjective.

daas-irab:22-24.t: ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَجِئْتَنا﴾ the hamza is for disapproving interrogation (al-istifhām al-inkārī), and a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿لِتَأْفِكَنا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit an after the lām of causation (taʿlīl); nā is its object and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before them. ﴿عَنْ آلِهَتِنا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿فَأْتِنا﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition), and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter; nā is its object and its fāʿil is latent; the clause is the apodosis of an implied condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿بِما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿تَعِدُنا﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿إِنْ﴾ a conditional particle causing the jussive. ﴿كُنْتَ﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, its khabar (predicate); the verbal clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted because what precedes it indicates it. ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil is latent, and the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّمَا﴾ a restraining particle and the restrained one (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿الْعِلْمُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿عِنْدَ﴾ an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), attached to an omitted khabar; the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَأُبَلِّغُكُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb and its first object, with its fāʿil latent. ﴿ما﴾ its second object. ﴿أُرْسِلْتُ﴾ a passive past verb and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَلكِنِّي﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and lākinna and its noun. ﴿أَراكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its first object, with its fāʿil latent. ﴿قَوْماً﴾ its second object; the clause arākum is the khabar of lākinnī. ﴿تَجْهَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of qawman. ﴿فَلَمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and mā is an adverbial conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. [Translator's note: so in the source ("mā"); the particle meant is lammā.] ﴿رَأَوْهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿عارِضاً﴾ an accusative ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿مُسْتَقْبِلَ﴾ an adjective of ʿāriḍan. ﴿أَوْدِيَتِهِمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the apodosis and has no grammatical position. ﴿هذا عارِضٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the nominal clause is the object of the saying. ﴿مُمْطِرُنا﴾ an adjective of ʿāriḍ. ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb). ﴿هُوَ مَا﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the nominal clause is the object of an omitted saying. ﴿اسْتَعْجَلْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿رِيحٌ﴾ a badal (substitute) of mā. ﴿فِيها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, a fronted khabar. ﴿عَذابٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿أَلِيمٌ﴾ an adjective; the nominal clause is an adjective of rīḥ.

daas-irab:25-27.t: ﴿تُدَمِّرُ﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿كُلَّ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is a second adjective (ṣifa) of rīḥ. ﴿بِأَمْرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿رَبِّها﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَأَصْبَحُوا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and aṣbaḥa and its noun. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يُرى﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿مَساكِنُهُمْ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause yurā is the khabar (predicate) of aṣbaḥū, and the clause fa-aṣbaḥū is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿نَجْزِي﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); its fāʿil is latent. ﴿الْقَوْمَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ an adjective; the verbal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is a particle of oath and of the genitive, the lām is [that of] the answer to the oath, and qad is a particle of realization (taḥqīq). ﴿مَكَّنَّاهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position. ﴿فِيما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿إِنْ﴾ redundant (zāʾida). ﴿مَكَّنَّاكُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿فِيهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿وَجَعَلْنا﴾ a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿سَمْعاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَأَبْصاراً وَأَفْئِدَةً﴾ both conjoined to samʿan. ﴿فَما﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and mā is negative. ﴿أَغْنى﴾ a past verb. ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿سَمْعُهُمْ﴾ the fāʿil of aghnā. ﴿وَلا أَبْصارُهُمْ وَلا أَفْئِدَتُهُمْ﴾ the words are conjoined to samʿuhum. ﴿مِنْ شَيْءٍ﴾ genitive in form, accusative in position, a mafʿūl muṭlaq; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb for past time, conveying the sense of causation (taʿlīl). ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿يَجْحَدُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of kānū, and the clause kānū is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿بِآياتِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَحاقَ﴾ a conjunction, and a past verb. ﴿بِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿ما﴾ fāʿil. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to yastahziʾūn. ﴿يَسْتَهْزِؤُنَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of kānū, and the clause kānū is the ṣila. ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ see the previous verse. ﴿أَهْلَكْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿ما﴾ its object. ﴿حَوْلَكُمْ﴾ an adverb of place (ẓarf makān). ﴿مِنَ الْقُرى﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَصَرَّفْنَا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿الْآياتِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ﴾ laʿalla and its noun. ﴿يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of laʿalla, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl).

daas-irab:28-30.t: ﴿فَلَوْلا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and lawlā is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). ﴿نَصَرَهُمُ﴾ a past verb and its object. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿اتَّخَذُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿قُرْباناً﴾ ḥāl; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿آلِهَةً﴾ the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb ittakhadhū. ﴿بَلْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿ضَلُّوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَذلِكَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿إِفْكُهُمْ﴾ khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَما﴾ conjoined to ifkuhum. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿يَفْتَرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of kānū. ﴿وَإِذْ﴾ a resumptive particle, and an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān). ﴿صَرَفْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿إِلَيْكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿نَفَراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِنَ الْجِنِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of nafaran. ﴿يَسْتَمِعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿الْقُرْآنَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿فَلَمَّا﴾ a conjunction, and lammā is an adverbial conditional particle. ﴿حَضَرُوهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿أَنْصِتُوا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause qālū is the apodosis of a condition that does not cause the jussive, and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَلَمَّا﴾ a conjunction, and lammā is an adverbial conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿قُضِيَ﴾ a passive past verb; its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿وَلَّوْا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position. ﴿إِلى قَوْمِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿مُنْذِرِينَ﴾ ḥāl. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يا قَوْمَنا﴾ the one addressed (munādā), annexed (muḍāf), accusative (manṣūb). ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿سَمِعْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿كِتاباً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the khabar of innā. ﴿أُنْزِلَ﴾ a passive past verb; its nāʾib fāʿil is latent, and the clause is an adjective of kitāban. ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿مُوسى﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مُصَدِّقاً﴾ an adjective of kitāban. ﴿لِما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to muṣaddiqan. ﴿بَيْنَ﴾ an adverb of place (ẓarf makān). ﴿يَدَيْهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿يَهْدِي﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent, and the clause is an adjective of kitāban. ﴿إِلَى الْحَقِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿وَإِلى طَرِيقٍ﴾ conjoined to what precedes them. ﴿مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾ an adjective of ṭarīq.

daas-irab:31-33.t: ﴿يا قَوْمَنا﴾ the one addressed (munādā), annexed (muḍāf), accusative (manṣūb). ﴿أَجِيبُوا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿داعِيَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَآمِنُوا﴾ conjoined to ajībū. ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿يَغْفِرْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab), with its fāʿil latent (mustatir). ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿مِنْ ذُنُوبِكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to the verb. ﴿وَيُجِرْكُمْ﴾ conjoined to yaghfir, and the kāf is its object. ﴿مِنْ عَذابٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿أَلِيمٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the verse is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ a resumptive particle, and man is a conditional noun causing the jussive, a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يُجِبْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), with its fāʿil latent. ﴿داعِيَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَلَيْسَ﴾ the fāʾ falls in the apodosis of the condition, and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿بِمُعْجِزٍ﴾ genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar (predicate) of laysa; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the clause man lā yujib is resumptive. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to muʿjiz; the two clauses of the protasis and the apodosis are the khabar of man. ﴿وَلَيْسَ﴾ a conjunction, and a defective past verb. ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿مِنْ دُونِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أَوْلِياءُ﴾ the postponed noun of laysa. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿فِي ضَلالٍ﴾ khabar. ﴿مُبِينٍ﴾ an adjective; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿أَوَلَمْ﴾ an interrogative particle, the wāw is a conjunction, and lam is a particle causing the jussive. ﴿يَرَوْا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive by lam, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ anna and its noun. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ an adjective. ﴿خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ﴾ a past verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent. ﴿وَالْأَرْضَ﴾ conjoined to al-samāwāt; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَلَمْ يَعْيَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and an imperfect verb, jussive by lam, with its fāʿil latent; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿بِخَلْقِهِنَّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿بِقادِرٍ﴾ the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and qādir is genitive in form, nominative in position, the khabar of anna; anna with its noun and its khabar stands in place of the two objects of yaraw. ﴿عَلى﴾ a preposition. ﴿أَنْ يُحْيِيَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by an, with its fāʿil latent. ﴿الْمَوْتى﴾ its object; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the preposition, and they [the preposition and its genitive noun] are attached to qādir. ﴿بَلى﴾ a particle of answer. ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿عَلى كُلِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to qadīr. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿قَدِيرٌ﴾ khabar; the nominal clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl).

daas-irab:34-35.t: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يُعْرَضُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا عَلَى النَّارِ﴾ its i'rab has preceded in verse 20. ﴿أَلَيْسَ﴾ the hamza is a particle of rebuking interrogation (istifhām tawbīkhī), and laysa is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿هذا﴾ its noun. ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar (predicate) of laysa; the clause is the object of an implied saying (maqūl qawl muqaddar). ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿بَلى﴾ a particle of answer; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَرَبِّنا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "we swear by our Lord" (nuqsimu bi-rabbinā). ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَذُوقُوا﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition), and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿الْعَذابَ﴾ its object; the clause is the apodosis of an implied condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿بِما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to dhūqū. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿تَكْفُرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of kuntum. ﴿فَاصْبِرْ﴾ a resumptive particle, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿كَما﴾ the kāf is a particle of comparison and of the genitive, and mā is maṣdariyya (yielding a verbal noun). ﴿صَبَرَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿أُولُوا﴾ fāʿil. ﴿الْعَزْمِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مِنَ الرُّسُلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, a ḥāl (circumstantial); mā and the verb are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the genitive by the kāf, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb. ﴿وَلا تَسْتَعْجِلْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, lā is prohibitive, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lā. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ﴾ kaʾanna and its noun. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān). ﴿يَرَوْنَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿يُوعَدُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive by lam, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar of kaʾanna, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿ساعَةً﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿مِنْ نَهارٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿بَلاغٌ﴾ the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "this Qur'an is a proclamation" (hādhā al-Qurʾān balāgh). ﴿فَهَلْ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and hal is an interrogative particle. ﴿يُهْلَكُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction. ﴿الْقَوْمُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿الْفاسِقُونَ﴾ an adjective.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿أَرَأَيْتُمْ مَّا تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ﴾, then He said: ﴿أَرُونِي مَاذَا خَلَقُواْ﴾ and did not say خلقت or خلقن, because He meant only the idols, so He made their action like the action of people and their like; for the idols are spoken to, worshipped, frequented and exalted as princes and their like are exalted, so He treated them like people.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] it is: مَن تعبدون من دون الله, making it (مَن); and this is an explicit statement of resemblance to people, in the verb and in the noun. And in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: أريتكم; and generally what is in his reading of the saying of Allah أريت and أريتم is, in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh, with kāf, so that in his reading there is even: "أرَيْتك الذى يُكذِّب بالدين".
His saying: ﴿أَوْ أَثَارَةٍ مِّنْ عِلْمٍ﴾.
The generality read it: "أثارة"; and some of them read it, he said: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read, as far as I know, "أثْرةً", light [without a vowel on the thāʾ]. And it is reported of some readers: "أثَرة". The meaning in all of them is: a remnant of knowledge, or something handed down (maʾthūr) from the books of the ancients.
Whoever reads "أثارة", it is like the maṣdar (verbal noun), as in your saying: al-samāḥa, al-shajāʿa.
Whoever reads "أَثَرة" built it on al-athar, as one says: qatara.
And whoever reads "أَثْرة", it is as though he meant something like His saying: ﴿إلا من خطِف الخطفة﴾, and al-rajfa.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَنْ أَضَلُّ مِمَّن يَدْعُواْ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَن لاَّ يَسْتَجِيبُ لَهُ﴾.
By (من) He meant the idols; and in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is: "مالا يستجيب له"; and this is of what I mentioned to you concerning من and ما.

farraa:9-9.t:
His saying: ﴿قُلْ مَا كُنتُ بِدْعاً مِّنَ ٱلرُّسُلِ﴾.
He says: I was not the first to be sent; many prophets were sent before me.
His saying: ﴿وَمَآ أَدْرِي مَا يُفْعَلُ بِي وَلاَ بِكُمْ﴾.
It was revealed concerning the Companions of the Prophet, Allah bless him. That was because they complained to him of what they were meeting from the people of Mecca before he was commanded to fight them. The Prophet, Allah bless him, said: "I have seen in my sleep that I emigrate to a land of palms, trees and water." They rejoiced at that; then they remained for a while without seeing it, and said to the Prophet, Allah bless him: "We do not see the fulfilment of what you said, while the harm has become severe on us." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down: ﴿قُلْ مَا كُنتُ بِدْعاً مِّنَ ٱلرُّسُلِ وَمَآ أَدْرِي مَا يُفْعَلُ بِي وَلاَ بِكُمْ﴾: will I go out to the place I was shown in my sleep or not? Then he said to them: "It is only something I was shown in my sleep, and I follow only what is revealed to me." He says: what I told you was not revealed to me; and had it been revelation, he, Allah bless him, would not have said: ﴿وَمَآ أَدْرِي مَا يُفْعَلُ بِي وَلاَ بِكُمْ﴾.

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿وَشَهِدَ شَاهِدٌ مِّن بَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ عَلَىٰ مِثْلِهِ.﴾.
A man of the Jews bore witness to the like of what ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām bore witness to, of confirming the Prophet, Allah bless him, and that he is described in the Torah; so that man believed while you were arrogant.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لَوْ كَانَ خَيْراً مَّا سَبَقُونَآ إِلَيْهِ﴾.
When Muzayna, Juhayna, Aslam and Ghifār embraced Islam, the Banū ʿĀmir ibn Ṣaʿṣaʿa, Ghaṭafān, Ashjaʿ and Asad said: "Had this been good, the herders of lambs would not have beaten us to it." This is the interpretation of His saying: ﴿لَوْ كَانَ خَيْراً مَّا سَبَقُونَآ إِلَيْهِ﴾.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿وَهَـٰذَا كِتَابٌ مُّصَدِّقٌ لِّسَاناً عَرَبِيّاً﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: مصدق لما بين يديه لسانا عربيا. Its accusative in our reading is according to the interpretation of ʿAbd Allāh's reading, i.e. this Qurʾān confirms the Torah, [being] clear Arabic. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it may be [accusative] from مصدق, as I explained to you, and it may be a qaṭʿ (detached ḥāl) from the hāʾ in بين يديه.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لِّيُنذِرَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ وَبُشْرَىٰ لِلْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾.
البشرى may be nominative or accusative. The nominative is on: "and this is a Book confirming, and good tidings"; and the accusative is on: "that you may warn those who did wrong and give good tidings (وتبشر)"; so when you drop تبشر and put in its place بشرى or بشارة, you use the accusative. Like it in speech: "I seek refuge with Allah from you", and "Watering (سقيا) to so-and-so", as though he said: "and may Allah water so-and-so"; and "I came to honour you, and as a visit (زيارة) to you and fulfilment (قضاء) of your right", whose meaning is: to visit you and fulfil your right; so you put الزيارة and القضاء in the accusative by an implied verb.

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying: ﴿وَوَصَّيْنَا ٱلإِنسَانَ بِوَالِدَيْهِ إِحْسَاناً﴾.
The people of Kūfa read it with the alif, and so it is in their codices; and the people of Medina and the people of Baṣra read: (حُسناً), and so it is in their codices; and their meaning is one, and Allah knows best.
His saying: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُ وَبَلَغَ أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: حتّى إذا استوى وبلغ أشده وبلغ أربعين سنة; and the meaning in it is like the meaning in our reading, because it is allowed in Arabic to say: "When a child was born to you and you reached the age of men, you sacrificed [the ʿaqīqa] and did such-and-such", while the reaching comes before the birth. And it is said that al-ashudd here is forty.
I heard one of the shaykhs mention, with an isnad of his, concerning al-ashudd: thirty-three, and concerning al-istiwāʾ: forty.
And I heard that al-ashudd in other than this place is eighteen. The first is more likely to be correct, because forty is closer in sequence to thirty-three than to eighteen. Do you not see that you say: "I took most of the wealth, or all of it", which is better than saying: "I took the least of the wealth, or all of it"? Like it is His saying: ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَعْلمُ أَنّكَ تقُومُ أَدْنَى مِنْ ثُلُثَىِ الّليْلِ وَنِصْفَهُ وَثُلُثَهُ﴾: some of these are close to others. This is the way of the speech of the Arabs [176/a]. And the second, meaning eighteen, [and] had it been joined to forty, would have been a valid view.
His saying: ﴿أَوْزِعْنِيۤ أَنْ أَشكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ﴾.
This verse was revealed concerning Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah have mercy on him.
[Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Ḥibbān ibn ʿAlī al-ʿAnazī narrated it to me, from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: it was revealed concerning Abū Bakr, may Allah have mercy on him, up to His saying: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِين نَتَقَبَّلُ عَنْهُمْ أَحْسَنَ﴾ to the end of the verse.
Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read, and it is reported of some of the companions of ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿نتقبَّلُ عنهم أحْسَنَ ما عَمِلوا ونتجاوز عن سيئاتهم﴾, with nūn. The reading of the generality is: "يُتقبل عنهم أحسن ما عملوا ويُتجاوز عن سيئاتهم", with yāʾ with ḍamma; and had it been read "تُتَقبَّل عنهم [أحسن ما عملوا] وتُتجاوز", it would have been correct.

farraa:16-16.t: His saying: ﴿وَعْدَ ٱلصِّدْقِ ٱلَّذِي﴾: like your saying "a true promise (وعدا صدقا)", annexed to itself. Whatever maṣdar is in the meaning of "truly (ḥaqqan)" is accusative, whether definite or indefinite, like His saying in Yūnus: ﴿وَعد الله حقّاً﴾.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِي قَالَ لِوَالِدَيْهِ أُفٍّ لَّكُمَآ﴾. It is reported that it was ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr who said this before he embraced Islam: (أُفٍّ لكما), "Filth to you both! Do you promise me that I shall be brought out of the grave?" The readers agreed on (أخرج) with ḍamma on the alif, its agent not named; and had it been read أن أَخْرُجَ, with fatḥa on the alif, it would have been correct.
His saying: ﴿وَهُمَا يَسْتَغثِيَانِ ٱللَّهَ﴾ and they say: "ويلك آمن". The verb of saying is implied; He means Abū Bakr, may Allah have mercy on him, and his wife.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْقَوْلُ﴾.
It was not revealed concerning ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr; rather, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said: "Raise up [for me] Judʿān ibn ʿAmr and ʿUthmān ibn ʿAmr" (and they were among his forefathers) "so that I may ask them about what Muḥammad, Allah bless him and grant him peace, says: is it true or false?" So Allah sent down: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْقَوْلُ﴾, meaning Judʿān and ʿUthmān.

farraa:20-20.t: His saying: ﴿أَذْهَبْتُمْ طَيِّبَاتِكُمْ﴾: al-Aʿmash, ʿĀṣim and Nāfiʿ of Medina read it without a question, and al-Ḥasan and Abū Jaʿfar of Medina read it with the question: "أأذهبتم". The Arabs use the question for rebuke, and also do not use the question, so they say: "You went and did such-and-such", and they say: "Did you go and do such-and-such?" And all is correct.

farraa:21-21.t:
His saying: ﴿إِذْ أَنذَرَ قَوْمَهُ بِٱلأَحْقَافِ﴾.
The aḥqāf of sand; its singular is ḥiqf, and the ḥiqf is the elongated sand-dune rising upward.
His saying: ﴿وَقَدْ خَلَتِ ٱلنُّذُرُ مِن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ﴾.
Before him, "and from behind him": after him; and it is [176/b] in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "من بين يديه ومن بعده".

farraa:24-24.t:
His saying: ﴿فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ عَارِضاً مُّسْتَقْبِلَ أَوْدِيَتِهِمْ﴾.
They hoped it would be rain-cloud, and said: "This is what you promised us; this, by Allah, is the rain and the good." Allah said: Say to them: rather, it is the punishment you sought to hasten. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: قل [بل] ما استعجلتم به هى ريح فيها عذاب أليم. And هو and هى in this place are in the position of His saying: "مِنْ مَنِىٍّ تُمْنَى" and "يمنى".
Whoever says "هو" refers to the punishment, and whoever says "هى" refers to the wind.

farraa:25-25.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأْصْبَحُواْ لاَ يُرَىٰ إِلاَّ مَسَاكِنُهُمْ﴾.
Al-Aʿmash, ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read it: "لا يُرَى إلا مساكنهم".
Al-Farrāʾ said: and ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah have mercy on him, read it.
[Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl al-Khurāsānī narrated to me, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, that he said: "لا تَرَى إلا مساكِنَهم".
[Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: and al-Kisāʾī narrated to me, from Qiṭr ibn Khalīfa, from Mujāhid, that he read: "فأصبحوا لا تَرى إلا مساكنهم". He said: and al-Ḥasan read: "فأصبحوا لا تُرى إلا مساكنُهم", and there is ugliness in it in Arabic, because the Arabs, when they put the verb of a feminine before إلا, make it masculine, saying: "None stood (لم يقم) but your slave-girl" and "None stood (ما قام) but your slave-girl", and they hardly say: "ما قامت إلا جاريتك". That is because what is left out is أحد (anyone), and أحد, whether it is for a feminine or a masculine, has a masculine verb. Do you not see that you say: "If anyone (أحد) of them (fem.) stands, strike him", and you do not say "if she stands" except under compulsion; and it is nevertheless allowed on that basis. He said: al-Mufaḍḍal recited to me:
وَنارنُا لم تُر ناراً مِثْلُها * قد عِلِمت ذكـَ ا معدّ أكْرما
(And our fire: no fire like it has been seen; Maʿadd has known [ours] to be the most generous.)
So he made the verb of (مثل) feminine because it is for the fire; and the best speech is to say: ما رُئى إلا مثلها.
«[Translator's note: the second hemistich is partly corrupt in the source («ذكـَ ا»); the gloss is tentative.]»

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ مَكَّنَاهُمْ فِيمَآ إِن مَّكَّنَّاكُمْ﴾.
He says: in that in which We have not established you; and (إن) is in the position of ما in negation (jaḥd).
His saying: ﴿وَحَاقَ بِهِم﴾.
In the speech of the Arabs it is: it came back upon them; and it came in the exegesis: it encompassed them and descended on them.

farraa:28-28.t:
His saying: ﴿وَذَلِكَ إِفْكُهُمْ وَمَا كَانُواْ يَفْتَرُونَ﴾.
It is also read أَفَكُهُم and أَفَكَهُم. As for al-ifk and al-afak, they are in the position of your saying: al-ḥidhr and al-ḥadhar, al-nijs and al-najas. And as for whoever says أَفكَهُم, he puts the hāʾ and mīm in the position of the accusative, saying: that turned them away from faith, and their lie; as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿يُؤفَكُ عنه مَن أُفِكَ﴾, i.e. he is turned away from it who is turned away.

farraa:33-33.t:
His saying: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ وَلَمْ يَعْيَ بِخَلْقِهِنَّ بِقَادِرٍ﴾.
The bāʾ entered because of لم. The Arabs bring it in with negation (al-juḥūd) when it puts what precedes it in the nominative, and they bring it in when a verb that needs two nouns falls upon it, as in your saying: "I do not think you are standing (بقائم)", and "I do not think that you are standing" [177/a], and "You were not standing". When you leave out the bāʾ, you put what it was in into the accusative by the verb that governs it; and had you dropped the bāʾ from قادر in this place, it would be nominative, because it is the khabar (predicate) of أنّ. He said: and one of them recited to me:
فما رَجعت بخائبةٍ رِكابٌ * حكيمُ بنُ المسيِّب مُنتهاها
(No riding camels whose destination was Ḥakīm ibn al-Musayyab ever came back disappointed.)
So he brought the bāʾ into a verb [i.e. a predicate] which, had it been dropped from it, would be accusative by the verb, not by the bāʾ. Analogize on this and what resembles it.
It is reported of some readers that he read (يَقدِر) in place of (بقادر), as Ḥamza read: "وَمَا أنتَ تهدى العمى", while the reading of the generality is: "بهادى العمى".

farraa:34-34.t:
His saying: ﴿أَلَيْسَ هَـٰذَا بِٱلْحَقِّ﴾.
In it there is an implied verb of saying: "it is said: is this not the truth?". بلاغٌ: i.e. "this is a proclamation", nominative by resumption (istiʾnāf).

zajjaj:3-3.t:
Sūrat al-Aḥqāf
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ما خَلَقْنا السَّماواتِ والأرْضَ وما بَيْنَهُما إلا بِالحَقِّ وأجَلٍ مُسَمًّى﴾: It has come in the exegesis: "We created them only for the truth," that is, for the establishment of the truth; and it may have the meaning: "The heavens and the earth stand only by the truth." And His saying right after this: ﴿والَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا عَمّا أُنْذِرُوا مُعْرِضُونَ﴾, that is, they turned away after the proof had been established for them by Allah's creation of the heavens and the earth and what is between them.

zajjaj:4-4.t:
Then He called them to the proof, for their sake, of the falsity of worshipping the idols they worship, and said: ﴿قُلْ أرَأيْتُمْ ما تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾. It is also read "أرَيْتُمْ", without alif. "ما تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ": "what you call upon as a god besides Allah." ﴿أرُونِي ماذا خَلَقُوا مِنَ الأرْضِ أمْ لَهم شِرْكٌ في السَّماواتِ﴾: that is, in the creation of the heavens; that is, so that for that reason you have made them partners in the worship of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
﴿ائْتُونِي بِكِتابٍ مِن قَبْلِ هَذا﴾: that is, "Bring me a book sent down containing proof of what you claim." ﴿أوْ أثارَةٍ مِن عِلْمٍ﴾: It is also read "أوْ أثَرَةٍ مِن عِلْمٍ", and it has been read "أوْ أثْرَةٍ مِن عِلْمٍ", with sukūn on the thāʾ. Its meaning, when one says "أثارَةٍ", is "a mark of knowledge"; it may also have the meaning "a remnant of knowledge"; and it may have the meaning "what is transmitted (yuʾthar) of knowledge."

zajjaj:5-5.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَن أضَلُّ مِمَّنْ يَدْعُو مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ مَن لا يَسْتَجِيبُ لَهُ إلى يَوْمِ القِيامَةِ وهم عَنْ دُعائِهِمْ غافِلُونَ﴾: that is, who is more astray than one who worships other than Allah?! Everything Allah has created is a proof of His oneness; so who is more astray than one who worships a stone that does not answer him? He said "وَمَن" and He said "وَهم", though it refers to what is not rational, because those who worshipped them treated them as things that discern, so they were addressed in accordance with their own way of speaking, as they said: ﴿ما نَعْبُدُهم إلا لِيُقَرِّبُونا إلى اللَّهِ زُلْفى﴾ [al-Zumar: 3]. Had it been "ما", that would have been good, as He said: ﴿لِمَ تَعْبُدُ ما لا يَسْمَعُ ولا يُبْصِرُ﴾ [Maryam: 42].

zajjaj:6-6.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإذا حُشِرَ النّاسُ كانُوا لَهم أعْداءً وكانُوا بِعِبادَتِهِمْ كافِرِينَ﴾: that is, the idols will disown their worship of them, saying: "We did not call them to worship us."

zajjaj:8-8.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ إنِ افْتَرَيْتُهُ فَلا تَمْلِكُونَ لِي مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئًا هو أعْلَمُ بِما تُفِيضُونَ فِيهِ﴾: that is, you have no power at all against Allah; that is, Allah has the greater power over His servants. ﴿كَفى بِهِ شَهِيدًا بَيْنِي وبَيْنَكُمْ﴾: that is, He suffices as a witness; "بِهِ" is in the position of the nominative. And His saying in this place: ﴿وَهُوَ الغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ﴾: its meaning is that whoever commits such of the great major sins as you have committed — fabricating lies against Allah, Majestic, Mighty and Exalted is He — and then repents, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful to him.

zajjaj:9-9.t:
And His saying: ﴿قُلْ ما كُنْتُ بِدْعًا مِنَ الرُّسُلِ﴾: that is, I was not the first to be sent; many messengers were sent before me.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَما أدْرِي ما يُفْعَلُ بِي ولا بِكم إنْ أتَّبِعُ إلا ما يُوحى إلَيَّ﴾: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had seen in his sleep that he would go to a land of palm trees and other trees, while his Companions had complained of the hardship that had befallen them. When he informed them that he would go to a land of palms and trees, and that was delayed, they thought what he, peace be upon him, had said was slow in coming. So he informed them that what he follows is what is revealed to him: if he is commanded to fight or to move, and that command is revelation, he follows it; and the dreams of the prophets, peace be upon them, are revelation.

zajjaj:10-10.t:
And His saying: ﴿قُلْ أرَأيْتُمْ إنْ كانَ مِن عِنْدِ اللَّهِ وكَفَرْتُمْ بِهِ وشَهِدَ شاهِدٌ مِن بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ عَلى مِثْلِهِ فَآمَنَ واسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ﴾: It has come in the exegesis «that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām came to the Prophet ﷺ and believed in him, and said to him: Ask the Jews about me, for they will commend me to you and tell you of my standing in knowledge. So the Prophet ﷺ asked them about him before they knew that he had believed, and they told him that he was the most knowledgeable of them in the Torah and in their doctrine, and that he was a scholar, son of a scholar, son of a scholar. Then he believed in their presence and bore witness that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah, and they said, after his believing: You are the worst of us and the son of the worst of us.
He said: Has it not come to you in the Torah from Moses, peace be upon him: When you see Muḥammad, convey my greeting of peace to him and believe in him?! And he set about showing them places in the Torah containing mention of the Prophet ﷺ and his description, while they were arrogant, denied, and deliberately covered that with their hands. And the answer (jawāb) of "إنْ كانَ مِن عِنْدِ اللَّهِ وكَفَرْتُمْ بِهِ وشَهِدَ شاهِدٌ مِن بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ عَلى مِثْلِهِ فَآمَنَ واسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ"»: "Will you believe?" «[Translator's note: i.e. the jawāb is implied as "أتُؤْمِنُونَ؟".]» Then He made known that these obstinate ones in particular would not believe, and said: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَهْدِي القَوْمَ الظّالِمِينَ﴾, that is, He has made their requital for their disbelief, after the guidance had become clear to them, His prolonging them in error. It has been said in the exegesis of His saying ﴿وَشَهِدَ شاهِدٌ مِن بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ عَلى مِثْلِهِ﴾: to the like of the testimony of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām; but the better view — and Allah knows best — is that "عَلى مِثْلِهِ" means "to the like of the testimony of the Prophet ﷺ."
«[Translator's note: in the source the closing quotation mark of the reported narration falls after the grammatical remark on the jawāb; it is kept where the source places it.]»

zajjaj:11-11.t: And His saying: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَوْ كانَ خَيْرًا ما سَبَقُونا إلَيْهِ﴾: It has come in the exegesis that when Juhayna, Muzayna, Aslam and Ghifār embraced Islam, Banū ʿĀmir, Ghaṭafān, Asad and Ashjaʿ said: If the religion these have entered were good, they would not have preceded us to it, for we are mightier than they; these are only herders of lambs.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِن قَبْلِهِ كِتابُ مُوسى إمامًا ورَحْمَةً﴾: "إمامًا" is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and His saying "وَرَحْمَةً" is conjoined to it. ﴿وَهَذا كِتابٌ مُصَدِّقٌ لِسانًا عَرَبِيًّا﴾: the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "and it confirms what was before it, in an Arabic tongue," because of what comes after this place: ﴿قالُوا يا قَوْمَنا إنّا سَمِعْنا كِتابًا أُنْـزِلَ مِن بَعْدِ مُوسى مُصَدِّقًا لِما بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ يَهْدِي إلى الحَقِّ﴾ [al-Aḥqāf: 30]. "لَهُ" (to it) has been omitted here — I mean from His saying "وَهَذا كِتابٌ مُصَدِّقٌ" — because before it is "وَمِن قَبْلِهِ كِتابُ مُوسى"; so the meaning is: "And this is a Book confirming it," that is, "confirming the Torah." And "لِسانًا عَرَبِيًّا" are both accusative as ḥāl; the meaning is: "confirming what was before it, being Arabic," and "لِسانًا" is mentioned for emphasis (tawkīd), as you say "جاءَنِي زَيْدٌ رَجُلًا صالِحًا" (Zayd came to me, a righteous man), meaning "Zayd came to me righteous," and you mention "رَجُلًا" for emphasis. There is another aspect in it, with the meaning: "And this is a Book confirming an Arabic tongue," the meaning being "confirming the Prophet, peace be upon him," so the meaning would be: "confirming one possessed of an Arabic tongue."
And His saying: ﴿لِيُنْذِرَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا﴾: It is also read "لِتُنْذِرَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا". ﴿وَبُشْرى لِلْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾: the better view is that "بُشْرى" is in the position of the nominative, the meaning being "and it is glad tidings for those who do good"; and it is possible that "بُشْرى" is in the position of the accusative, with the meaning: "to warn those who do wrong and to give the doers of good glad tidings."

zajjaj:13-13.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ قالُوا رَبُّنا اللَّهُ ثُمَّ اسْتَقامُوا فَلا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: the meaning of "ثُمَّ اسْتَقامُوا" is: they remained steadfast upon the oneness of Allah and the law of His Prophet, peace be upon him.

zajjaj:15-15.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَوَصَّيْنا الإنْسانَ بِوالِدَيْهِ إحْسانًا﴾: It is also read "حُسْنًا", and both are good. "إحْسانًا" is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of "وَصَّيْناهُ بِوالِدَيْهِ" is: We commanded him to do good to them with goodness.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حَمَلَتْهُ أُمُّهُ كُرْهًا﴾, and "كَرْهًا" — both have been read. The meaning is: "His mother carried him with hardship and delivered him with hardship."
And His saying: ﴿وَحَمْلُهُ وفِصالُهُ ثَلاثُونَ شَهْرًا﴾: It has been read "وَفَصْلُهُ ثَلاثُونَ شَهْرًا". The meaning of "فِصالُهُ" is his weaning. The least that pregnancy can be is six months. The preferred [reading] is "وَفِصالُهُ", because what has come in the hadith is: «"There is no suckling after al-fiṣāl,"» meaning after weaning.
And His saying: ﴿حَتّى إذا بَلَغَ أشُدَّهُ وبَلَغَ أرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً﴾: It has come in the exegesis that "al-ashudd" (full strength) is thirty-three years; it has been said: al-ashudd is eighteen years; and it has been said: al-ashudd is reaching puberty. The prevailing view is that it is thirty-three, because the time at which a person becomes complete in his body, his strength and the firmness of his youth is when he reaches thirty-odd years, and likewise in his discernment.
And His saying: ﴿وَأصْلِحْ لِي في ذُرِّيَّتِي﴾: its meaning is: make my offspring righteous.

zajjaj:16-16.t:
And His saying: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ نَتَقَبَّلُ عَنْهم أحْسَنَ ما عَمِلُوا﴾: "أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ يُتَقَبَّلُ عَنْهم أحْسَنُ ما عَمِلُوا" is also permissible. The reading is "يُتَقَبَّلُ" and "نَتَقَبَّلُ", and likewise "يُتَجاوَزُ" and "نَتَجاوَزُ". "يَتَقَبَّلُ" is permissible, but I do not know of anyone who read it so.
And His saying: ﴿وَعْدَ الصِّدْقِ الَّذِي كانُوا يُوعَدُونَ﴾: this is accusative because it is a maṣdar confirming what precedes it (maṣdar muʾakkid), because His saying ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ نَتَقَبَّلُ عَنْهم أحْسَنَ ما عَمِلُوا﴾ has the meaning of a promise, since Allah has promised them acceptance; so "وَعْدَ الصِّدْقِ" is an emphasis (tawkīd) of that.

zajjaj:17-17.t:
And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿والَّذِي قالَ لِوالِدَيْهِ أُفٍّ لَكُما﴾: It has been read "أُفِّ لَكُما" and "أُفَّ لَكُما"; we have explained that in Sūrat Banī Isrāʾīl.
And His saying: ﴿أتَعِدانِنِي أنْ أُخْرَجَ﴾: It is also read "أنْ أخْرُجَ" (that I will come out). "أتَعِدانِّي" with assimilation (idghām) is also permissible; or, if you wish, you pronounce both nūns distinctly; and if you wish you give the yāʾ sukūn, and if you wish you give it fatḥa. It has been transmitted from some of them as "أتَعِدانَنِي", with fatḥa, but that is a solecism (laḥn) with no justification, so do not ever read it so, because giving fatḥa to the nūn of the dual is an error; even if that is reported as an anomaly (shudhūdh), a reading is not to be based on anomaly. It is reported that His saying in the verse before this, up to His saying ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ نَتَقَبَّلُ عَنْهُمْ﴾ [al-Aḥqāf: 16], was revealed concerning Abū Bakr, may Allah have mercy on him. As for His saying ﴿والَّذِي قالَ لِوالِدَيْهِ أُفٍّ لَكُما﴾, some of them said it was revealed concerning ʿAbd al-Raḥmān [ibn Abī Bakr] before his embracing Islam; but this is invalidated by
«[Translator's note: the sentence continues in the next entry (al-Aḥqāf 18).]»

zajjaj:18-18.t: His saying: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ القَوْلُ في أُمَمٍ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ مِنَ الجِنِّ والإنْسِ إنَّهم كانُوا خاسِرِينَ﴾: for Allah made known that the word of punishment has become due upon these; and when He made that known, He made known that they will not believe. But ʿAbd al-Raḥmān was a believer, among the most excellent of the believers and their nobles. The correct exegesis is that it was revealed concerning the undutiful disbeliever.

zajjaj:19-19.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلِكُلٍّ دَرَجاتٌ مِمّا عَمِلُوا ولِيُوَفِّيَهم أعْمالَهُمْ﴾, and "وَلِنُوَفِّيَهم" — both [are read], with nūn and with yāʾ.

zajjaj:20-20.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يُعْرَضُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا عَلى النّارِ﴾: Most of the readers have fatḥa on the nūn and tafkhīm (full, unslanted pronunciation) in "اَلنّارِ"; but most of the speech of the Arabs inclines the alif towards kasra (imāla), and Abū ʿAmr reads so: "عَلى النِّارِ". He prefers the kasra on the rāʾ because the rāʾ, according to them, is a repeated (trilled) letter, so its kasra is as though it were two kasras.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أذْهَبْتُمْ طَيِّباتِكُمْ﴾: without the interrogative alif; and it is read "أأذْهَبْتُمْ" with two fully pronounced hamzas, and with two hamzas of which the second is lightened. This alif is for rebuke (tawbīkh); in rebuke you may retain the alif if you wish, or omit it if you wish, as you say: "يا فُلانُ أحْدَثْتَ ما لا يَحِلُّ لَكَ؟ جَنَيْتَ عَلى نَفْسِكَ" (O so-and-so, you have done what is not lawful for you? You have wronged yourself), when you rebuke him; or, if you wish: "أأخَذْتَ ما لا يَحِلُّ لَكَ؟ أجَنَيْتَ عَلى نَفْسِكَ؟" (Did you take what is not lawful for you? Did you wrong yourself?).
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فاليَوْمَ تُجْزَوْنَ عَذابَ الهُونِ﴾: its meaning is: al-hawān (humiliation).
«[Translator's note: "fatḥa on the nūn" is as in the source; in context the point concerns the alif of "النّار" (no imāla), and the source may intend that.]»

zajjaj:21-21.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿واذْكُرْ أخا عادٍ إذْ أنْذَرَ قَوْمَهُ بِالأحْقافِ﴾: "اَلْأحْقافُ" are long, raised sand-dunes like mounds; these aḥqāf were the dwellings of ʿĀd.
And His saying: ﴿وَقَدْ خَلَتِ النُّذُرُ مِن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ ومِن خَلْفِهِ ألا تَعْبُدُوا إلا اللَّهَ﴾: that is, they had been warned of punishment if they worshipped other than Allah, in what preceded before Hūd's warning, and on the tongue of Hūd, peace be upon him: ﴿إنِّي أخافُ عَلَيْكم عَذابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾ ﴿قالُوا أجِئْتَنا لِتَأْفِكَنا عَنْ آلِهَتِنا﴾ [al-Aḥqāf: 22], that is, to turn us away from them by falsehood and lying. ﴿فَأْتِنا بِما تَعِدُنا﴾ [al-Aḥqāf: 22], that is, bring us the punishment you promise us, ﴿إنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الصّادِقِينَ﴾ [al-Aḥqāf: 22].

zajjaj:23-23.t: ﴿قالَ إنَّما العِلْمُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾: that is, He knows when the punishment will come to you. ﴿وَأُبَلِّغُكم ما أُرْسِلْتُ بِهِ﴾: it is also read with the lighter form: "وَأُبْلِغُكُمِ". ﴿وَلَكِنِّي أراكم قَوْمًا تَجْهَلُونَ﴾: that is, I direct you to right guidance while you turn away and worship gods that neither benefit nor harm.

zajjaj:24-24.t:
And His saying: ﴿فَلَمّا رَأوْهُ عارِضًا مُسْتَقْبِلَ أوْدِيَتِهِمْ﴾: that is, when they saw the cloud from which arose the wind with which they were punished spread across the sky, they said: What you promised us is a cloud containing rain, life and showers. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿بَلْ هو ما اسْتَعْجَلْتُمْ بِهِ رِيحٌ فِيها عَذابٌ ألِيمٌ﴾. Some read: "قُلْ بَلْ هو ما اسْتَعْجَلْتُمْ". The wind, from its violence, would lift the shepherd together with his sheep; and so Allah destroyed the people of ʿĀd with that wind.
And His saying: ﴿مُمْطِرُنا﴾: its form is the form of a definite noun, but it is an adjective (ṣifa) of an indefinite one; the meaning is: "عارِضٌ مُمْطِرٌ إيّانا" (a cloud raining upon us), except that "إيّانا" is not detached here.

zajjaj:25-25.t:
And His saying: ﴿فَأصْبَحُوا لا يُرى إلا مَساكِنُهُمْ﴾: There are five aspects in this. The best of them in Arabic and in reading is "لا يُرى إلّا مَساكِنُهم", its interpretation being "nothing was seen except their dwellings," because they had been destroyed. "فَأصْبَحُوا لا تُرى إلّا مَساكِنُهم" is also permissible, the meaning then being "no figures were seen except their dwellings." It is also read "فَأصْبَحُوا تَرى مَساكِنَهم", that is, "you see nothing but their dwellings." And there are two aspects in it with the alif omitted: "فَأصْبَحُوا لا يُرى إلّا مَسْكَنُهم" and "مَسْكَنَهم"; and "فَأصْبَحُوا لا تَرى إلّا مَسْكَنَهم" is permissible. One says "سَكَنَ، يَسْكُنُ، مَسْكَنًا، ومَسْكِنًا".
«[Translator's note: the third reading appears in the source as "فَأصْبَحُوا تَرى مَساكِنَهم", without "لا… إلّا", though it is glossed with them.]»
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَذَلِكَ نَجْزِي القَوْمَ المُجْرِمِينَ﴾: the meaning is "Like that We requite the criminal people," that is, with punishment.

zajjaj:26-26.t: And His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ مَكَّنّاهم فِيما إنْ مَكَّنّاكم فِيهِ﴾: "إنْ" here has the meaning of "ما" (negation). "إنْ" for negation together with "ما" that has the meaning of "اَلَّذِي" (that which) is better in sound than "ما". Do you not see that if you said "رَغِبْتُ فِيما ما رَغِبْتَ فِيهِ", it would be better to say "قَدْ رَغِبْتُ فِيما إنْ رَغِبْتَ فِيهِ", meaning "in that which you did not desire," because of the difference between the two words.

zajjaj:28-28.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلْ ضَلُّوا عَنْهم وذَلِكَ إفْكُهُمْ﴾: that is, "their calling upon their gods is their falsehood (ifk)." It is also read "أفَكَهم", with the meaning "and that is their lying and their disbelief"; "اَلْأفْكُ" and "اَلْأفَكُ" are like "اَلنَّجْسُ" and "اَلنَّجَسُ". And it is read "أفَكَهم" [as a verb], that is, "that made them astray, disbelieving," that is, turned them away from the truth. And it is read "آفَكَهم", that is, "made them utter falsehood," as you say: "That made them disbelieve and led them astray."

zajjaj:29-29.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإذْ صَرَفْنا إلَيْكَ نَفَرًا مِنَ الجِنِّ يَسْتَمِعُونَ القُرْآنَ فَلَمّا حَضَرُوهُ قالُوا أنْصِتُوا﴾: that is, they said to one another: "صَهْ", and the meaning of "صَهْ" is "be silent." It is said that they were nine persons, or seven persons, and among them was Zawbaʿa. ﴿فَلَمّا قُضِيَ ولَّوْا إلى قَوْمِهِمْ مُنْذِرِينَ﴾: that is, when the Qur'an was recited to them until it was finished, they turned back to their people as warners. It is also read "فَلَمّا قَضاهُ" (when he finished it).

zajjaj:30-30.t: ﴿قالُوا يا قَوْمَنا إنّا سَمِعْنا كِتابًا أُنْـزِلَ مِن بَعْدِ مُوسى مُصَدِّقًا لِما بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾: that is, it confirms all the books that preceded it and the prophets who brought them. In this is a proof that the Prophet ﷺ was sent to mankind and the jinn.

zajjaj:33-33.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أنَّ اللَّهَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ والأرْضَ ولَمْ يَعْيَ بِخَلْقِهِنَّ بِقادِرٍ عَلى أنْ يُحْيِيَ المَوْتى﴾: The bāʾ entered the khabar (predicate) of "إنَّ" because of the entry of "أوَلَمْ" at the beginning of the speech. If you said "ظَنَنْتُ أنَّ زَيْدًا بِقائِمٍ", it would not be permissible; but if you said "ما ظَنَنْتُ أنَّ زَيْدًا بِقائِمٍ", it would be permissible, because of the entry of "ما". The entry of "أنَّ" is only emphasis (tawkīd) of the speech; so it is as though its implied form (taqdīr) were: "Is not Allah able to give life to the dead, in what you see and in what you know?!" It has also been read "يَقْدِرُ عَلى أنْ يُحْيِيَ المَوْتى"; the first is the reading which most of the readers follow, but this one is also permissible.

zajjaj:35-35.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فاصْبِرْ كَما صَبَرَ أُولُو العَزْمِ مِنَ الرُّسُلِ﴾: It has come in the exegesis that the possessors of resolve are "Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus and Muḥammad," Allah's blessings be upon them all.
His saying: ﴿لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا إلا ساعَةً مِن نَهارٍ بَلاغٌ﴾: The nominative is with the meaning "that is a proclamation (balāgh)." The accusative is good and sound in Arabic, except that it contradicts the codex; "بَلاغًا" would be with the meaning "they proclaim a proclamation," as He said: ﴿كِتابَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 24], which is accusative on the meaning of "حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكم أُمَّهاتُكم" (forbidden to you are your mothers), its interpretation being "Allah has prescribed that as a prescription."
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَهَلْ يُهْلَكُ إلا القَوْمُ الفاسِقُونَ﴾: its interpretation is that — given Allah's mercy and bounty — none will perish except the defiantly disobedient people. Had it been read "فَهَلْ يَهْلِكُ إلّا القَوْمُ الفاسِقُونَ", it would be a valid aspect, but I know of no one who read it so. There is nothing in [the Qur'an] giving stronger hope for Allah's mercy than this verse, namely His saying: ﴿فَهَلْ يُهْلَكُ إلا القَوْمُ الفاسِقُونَ﴾.
